mainEntity.name: How do I know if my implant dentist is qualified?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can verify that any dental professional is registered with the General Dental Council (GDC) using the publicly available online register at gdc-uk.org. Beyond basic registration, you may also ask your dentist directly about their postgraduate training in implantology, the professional bodies or associations they are affiliated with, and their experience placing implants. A confident and ethical implant dentist will welcome these questions and answer them openly.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal to feel nervous about dental implant treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — feeling apprehensive about any surgical dental procedure is entirely understandable and very common. A good implant dentist will take time to address your concerns, explain each step of the process clearly, and make you feel comfortable before proceeding. Practices experienced in treating anxious patients can often offer additional support measures. Never feel embarrassed about discussing nerves with your dental team — doing so helps them tailor their approach to your needs.

mainEntity.name: What should a dental implant consultation include?

acceptedAnswer.text: A thorough dental implant consultation should include a review of your medical and dental history, an examination of your teeth, gums, and bite, and appropriate imaging such as X-rays or a CBCT scan to assess bone structure. Your dentist should discuss whether implants are suitable for you, explain what the treatment involves, outline expected timelines and costs, and give you the opportunity to ask questions. Treatment should not be recommended without a proper clinical assessment.

mainEntity.name: Can teeth grinding affect a dental implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — bruxism (teeth grinding or jaw clenching) can place excessive force on dental implants and their restorations over time, potentially contributing to crown wear or stress on the implant structure. If you grind your teeth, it is important to discuss this with your implant dentist before and after treatment. A custom-fitted night guard (occlusal splint) may be recommended to help protect your restoration during sleep. This is a routine and sensible preventative measure for many implant patients.

mainEntity.name: How long does dental implant treatment typically take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treatment timelines vary significantly depending on individual clinical circumstances. Some patients may be suitable for same-day or immediate implant placement, while others may require preparatory treatment — such as bone grafting or gum disease management — before implant placement can begin. The osseointegration healing phase alone typically takes between six weeks and several months. Your dentist should provide a realistic, individualised timeline as part of your written treatment plan.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I have concerns about my implant dentist mid-treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you have concerns at any stage of your implant treatment, it is appropriate to raise them directly with your dental practice in the first instance. Most concerns can be resolved through open communication. If you remain unhappy, you are entitled to seek a second opinion from another qualified dental professional. You may also contact the Dental Complaints Service (for private treatment) or the General Dental Council if you believe standards of care have not been met.
